provenance: Every value below is what the L4 encoding answered; nothing here is computed in JavaScript.

scenarios.label: Spouse, no children — with a flat
scenarios.story: Married, no children, both parents gone. The HDB flat and the savings.
scenarios.note: ISA s 4-5: the deceased was domiciled in Singapore, so this Act regulates the whole Singapore estate.

shares.basis: ISA s 7 rule 1 -- spouse takes the whole estate

scenarios.whatHappensNext: There is no will, so the estate passes on intestacy. A person entitled to a share applies to the Family Justice Courts for LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION (PAA s 18). Priority follows entitlement to the estate under ISA s 7. Apply within 6 months of the death, or the Public Trustee may be granted them instead (PAA s 55(1)(a)).

timeline.event: the death of the deceased
timeline.basis: PAA s 37: on an intestacy, and on a testacy where no executor has power to obtain probate, the real and personal estate vests in the Public Trustee from this date until a grant of administration is made.

timeline.event: 6 months from the death: if no application for probate or letters of administration has been made, letters of administration may be granted to the Public Trustee or to such other person as the court thinks fit
timeline.basis: PAA s 55(1)(a). By PAA s 55(2) the Public Trustee is not prevented from applying before this date.

timeline.event: the grant is made
timeline.basis: PAA s 28(1): upon the grant the grantee takes an oath faithfully to administer the estate and to account for it, unless the grantee is the Public Trustee or a trust company (s 28(2)). PAA s 37(4): the estate ceases to be vested in the Public Trustee.

timeline.event: one month from the grant: security lawfully required must have been given, or letters of administration may be granted to the Public Trustee
timeline.basis: PAA s 55(1)(c), read with PAA s 29(7) and s 29(8) on when security is required at all.

timeline.event: 6 months from the date the grant is first made: last date for an application to rectify the will without the permission of a court
timeline.basis: WA 1838 s 28(2). The court may permit a later application; WA s 28(3) protects personal representatives who distribute after this date.

scenarios.label: A Muslim estate
scenarios.story: Section 2 puts this outside the Act entirely. The tool refuses rather than answering.
scenarios.note: ISA s 2: this Act does not apply to the estate of a Muslim. The estate is governed by Muslim law and the Administration of Muslim Law Act 1966; a faraid distribution is outside this encoding.
scenarios.whatHappensNext: The estate is distributed under Muslim law. Apply to the Syariah Court for an inheritance certificate, then to the Family Justice Courts for letters of administration. The Intestate Succession Act does not apply (ISA s 2).
scenarios.governingAct: Muslim law and the Administration of Muslim Law Act 1966 — not the Intestate Succession Act 1967 (ISA s 2).
